title: Defensive schema guards, runtime fallback, and observability acceptance
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Define acceptance criteria and operational playbooks for structured responses and tool/function calling when emitted as progressive/streamed frames. Emphasis on defensive schema validation, runtime fallback behavior under partial or malformed emissions, and telemetry that enables automated repair suggestions and post-incident analysis.
background: We have multiple customers using streamed structured outputs with tool invocations. Edge cases with partial frames, schema drift, and intermediate parse failures are creating production incidents. Current solutions rely on client-side heuristics and inconsistent operator runbooks. This work creates a defensive contract and observable signals so runtime, SDKs, and Console can coordinate safe fallbacks and remediation.
goals: Define a minimal, implementable schema envelope that supports versioning and soft-parse modes
Specify runtime fallback semantics for: malformed frames, incomplete tool-handshakes, and KV cache loss
Enumerate telemetry and traces required to diagnose partial-output incidents and recommend automated repair actions
Provide a clear acceptance test matrix (unit, e2e, chaos) that engineering can implement and QA can run
in_scope: Envelope format and versioning header for streamed structured output
Frame-level acknowledgement semantics and checkpoint hashes
Runtime automatic fallback policies (best-effort JSON vs. fail-fast vs. buffered-retry)
SDK soft-parse behavior and developer configuration knobs
Telemetry events, tracing spans, and Console UI signals for partial-emission incidents
Operator playbook for triage and automated suggested remediation
out_of_scope: Changes to model generation logic (prompt engineering or model fine-tuning)
Major schema redesigns for existing stable products that would require client migrations
acceptance_criteria: Envelope header present: every streamed response must start with a single-line JSON header with fields: envelope_version, request_id, timestamp, and schema_hint; header parsing must be robust to leading whitespace
Backward-compatible version negotiation: runtime accepts envelope_version values it knows and returns a clear 'unsupported_envelope_version' error frame when not compatible
Frame ACKs: runtime emits deterministic frame-level ACK events (ack, seq, cumulative_hash). ACKs are emitted within 200ms of frame commit under normal load

Soft-parse fallback: when a streamed frame fails strict JSON parse, SDK/runtime must expose a 'soft_parse' representation (lossy string-wrapped fragments) and emit a structured telemetry event marking 'soft_parse' with failure_reason

Graceful tool-call degradation: if a tool handshake does not complete within handshake_timeout, runtime must either (configurable) 1) fallback to a no-op tool stub, 2) return partial-result envelope with tool_error metadata, or 3) retry handshake using preconfigured alternate endpoint; chosen policy must be honored and observable

Checkpointed resume: client can request resume from last-acknowledged seq and runtime must be able to replay subsequent frames for 72 hours for Dedicated and 24 hours for Hosted (configurable per plan)

Idempotency guarantees for tool calls: when a function is invoked as part of a streamed envelope, it must include an idempotency_key derived from request_id+seq; downstream tool adapters must surface duplicate-detection metadata

Test coverage: unit tests for header parsing, ACK emission, and soft-parse creation; integration tests that inject malformed frames and confirm fallback policy execution; chaos tests that drop random frames and validate resume behavior

Telemetry completeness: for each partial-output or tool-handshake failure an event is emitted with tags: request_id, user_id (if available), route, model, envelope_version, seq_start, seq_end, failure_reason, handler_policy

Operator runbook: documented Console playbook accessible from incident summary that recommends 1-3 remediation steps and the Console shows suggested action buttons (retry, promote alternate tool, escalate to on-call)
SDK parity: JavaScript and Python SDKs implement the same soft-parse API and expose a clear opt-in toggle for strict vs soft parsing
testing_plan: Unit: header parser fuzz-tests (10k random inputs), frame ACK timing assertions
Integration: end-to-end streaming with instrumented tool adapters; inject malformed frames, slow handshakes, and KV cache clear in mid-flight
Chaos: service-level chaos injection (network partition, instance preemption) to ensure resume & checkpointing works for configured retention windows
Client compatibility matrix: run JS/Python SDKs against runtime flags (strict/soft) and validate behavior using automation harness
Manual QA: scripted scenarios and acceptance checklist to be executed by QA before canary rollout
rollout_plan: Feature flag: behind runtime feature flag and SDK opt-in; default to safe legacy behavior for 2 weeks
Canary: enable for 1% of production traffic in a single region for 48 hours; expand to 10% with monitoring gating
Gradual ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 7 days subject to no Sev1/Sev2 incidents and stability metrics
Console/Docs: ship operator playbook and SDK migration guide concurrently with 10% canary
telemetry_and_alerting: Metric: tool_handshake_time_p95 (alert if exceeds SLO by 2x)
Trace: end-to-end span with envelope_version and seq ranges for sampled requests
Event: partial_emit_failure with tags outlined in acceptance criteria
Dashboard: per-route breakdown of parse_mode (strict|soft), partial_emit_rate, resume_success_rate
dependencies: runtime team (engine changes for ACKs and envelope headers): ENG-40212
SDK team (JS + Python soft-parse APIs): ENG-41877
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: increased telemetry volume leading to billing spikes; Mitigation: sample partial_emit events at 10% by default and upsample on anomaly
Risk: client confusion between strict and soft parsing; Mitigation: clear SDK defaults and migration docs with code examples
Risk: resume storage growth; Mitigation: retention windows configurable per plan and gc policy enforced by infra
Risk: accidental duplicate tool side-effects from retries; Mitigation: require idempotency_key on function calls and surface duplicate-detection to clients
operator_playbook_summary: When Console shows a partial-emission incident: 1) review partial_emit_failure event and seq ranges; 2) choose recommended action (retry/resume/promote alternate tool); 3) if resume fails, escalate to runtime on-call with provided traces and cumulative_hash
